change_management_approach: Meridian manages scope and change through a lightweight, documented change-control process: any request outside the agreed baseline is logged, assessed for schedule/cost/risk impact, and reviewed jointly with the client's project sponsor before work begins. Approved changes are tracked in the same project management system used for day-to-day delivery, so the client always has a single, current view of scope, schedule, and budget impact.
performance_optimization_approach: Performance is treated as a first-class, measurable requirement rather than a post-launch concern: target response times and load thresholds are agreed during design, validated through load testing before go-live, and monitored continuously afterward via the same observability stack used for production support (metrics, tracing, and alerting), with a documented tuning process for any metric that drifts outside its agreed threshold.
maintenance_and_support: Following go-live, Meridian provides a defined warranty period (typically 90 days) with defect remediation at no additional cost, followed by an ongoing maintenance agreement covering security patching, dependency updates, minor enhancements, and a monitored support queue staffed during agreed business hours (with 24/7 coverage available for critical-severity issues where contracted).
operating_support_model: Support requests are received through a dedicated ticketing queue tied to the SLA tiers below, triaged by severity, and routed to the engineer(s) most familiar with the affected component. A named Technical Account Lead maintains continuity between the delivery team and the client's IT staff, and a monthly service review covers ticket volume, SLA adherence, and any recurring issues worth addressing at the root cause.
